methods.note: The paper-level method claims are supported: HotSpot 6.0 steady-state on page 4 and page 7, TED+SCBO on pages 7-9, and design-time-only thermal management with DVFS rejected on page 3. The reproduction framing is not supported. The extraction sets kind=custom_2d_steady and steady_2d_relevant=true, but the paper models a 2.5D stack (interposer, BEOL, micro-bumps, TIM, spreader, heat sink, distributed NoP power, separate compute and I/O dies). The extraction itself lists these as essential mismatches. A 2D steady model cannot be called a reproduction of this setup.

code.note: The 14 pages of text contain no repository, code, availability statement or supplementary link. The assets list is empty. The simulator, HotSpot driver and BoTorch SCBO code are not available, so no code claim can be verified.

parameters.note: The scalar values are supported by the text: Table IV 'Ours' row (74.8 C, 59.8 mJ, 2.01 ms, 0.911, 132.2, 5x4 cores, 1x2 chiplets, 2.3 mm ICS, 240 GB/s, 1024 KB, 208x112). The 75 C and 300 mm2 constraints, 45 C ambient, 0.4 K/W convection, 1.8 GHz and 128 GB/s DRAM are on page 9. The 49%, 14.2% and 17.6% area shares are on page 12. The unit conversions are arithmetically correct. Three points are weakened. HotSpot material and layer values are only cited from TESA [12]. The reading of 17.6% as the ICS gap is an inference. The axis assignment of 5x4 is unknown. No physical dimension or per-block power parameter exists.

config.note: No HotSpot config, floorplan file, layer stack, material table or boundary-condition file is published or pinned. The 0.4 K/W convection resistance cannot be mapped to a specific model layer without those files. The extraction correctly leaves experiment.floorplan and power_w empty, so there is no runnable configuration.

data.note: The paper publishes no per-block coordinates, dimensions or power for the selected design. Only totals (59.8 mJ, 2.01 ms) and graphics (Fig. 10(a), Fig. 10(b)) are given. No same-scenario power exists for any floorplan block, and the floorplan is empty. The supplied evidence is text only, with no figure images, so the decisive figures (Fig. 10 area breakdown and thermal map, Fig. 8, Fig. 11) were not visually verified. The 74.8 C observable is verified from Table IV text, but nothing in the packet can support a numeric comparison.

findings.reason: The extraction marks the case as 2D steady-relevant with kind custom_2d_steady, yet the paper's setup is a 2.5D interposer/BEOL/TIM/heat-spreader/heat-sink stack with distributed NoP power. The extraction's own essential mismatches contradict this. Calling a 2D run a reproduction would be unsupported.
findings.locator: PDF p.7 Fig. 6 and Sec. IV.C.4; extraction.physical_mismatches[1]; extraction.thermal_observable

findings.reason: The floorplan is empty. No block names, x/y or width/height are published, and Fig. 10 was not digitized. There are no floorplan blocks to which same-scenario power could be attached.

There is no per-block power. Table IV gives only total energy and delay, and the average-power rule (Eq. 19) is not applied per block. Any split would be an arbitrary assumption rather than paper evidence.
findings.locator: PDF p.7 Eq. 19; PDF p.10 Table IV 'Ours'

findings.reason: No pinned assets, linked artifacts, HotSpot config or code were supplied. A bare absence of links cannot support any code or config claim.

Fig. 10(a) area breakdown and Fig. 10(b) thermal map are cited as evidence, but only caption text was supplied and no rendered image was reviewed. Fig. 8 and Fig. 11 are likewise unverified. The quantitative claims drawn from the text (49%, 14.2%, 17.6%) were not cross-checked against the figure.
findings.locator: PDF p.11 Fig. 8; PDF p.12 Fig. 10 and Fig. 11

findings.reason: The extraction states the 17.6% 'is the ICS gap', but the paper only says it is 'reserved for cooling structures'. The identification is an inference, and the paper itself does not define the base area (chip vs interposer).
The per-chiplet core split (about 10 cores each) and the axis mapping of 5x4 versus 1x2 are inferred. The paper gives neither, so any geometry derived from them is not paper-derived.
findings.locator: PDF p.10 Table IV 'Ours'; extraction.evidence chiplet_partition

findings.reason: The 0.4 K/W convection and 45 C ambient are stated. TIM, spreader, heat-sink and interposer properties and thicknesses are only cited from TESA [12] and are not given numerically, so the thermal boundary model cannot be reconstructed.
findings.locator: PDF p.7 Sec. IV.C.4; PDF p.9 Sec. V.A

findings.reason: The paper contains internal discrepancies that were not flagged. The Table V ThermoDSE EDYP is 132.4 against 132.2 in Table IV. The Fig. 8 text gives the best scanned design at 256 GB/s against 240 GB/s in Table IV. These are minor but show scenario values must be tied strictly to Table IV. Table IV EDYP also uses unstated units.
findings.locator: PDF p.12 Table V; PDF p.11 Sec. V.E; PDF p.10 Table IV
